thread:
mike: Hey — spotted a weird billing spike for acct acme-inc during a streaming request. looks related to a reconnect + truncation path. anyone seen this pattern before?
ashley: ugh. seen similar once. details? truncated stream + client reconnect?
ravi: pinging logs now. can you paste the request id / session id?
mike: session=abc123, model=redwood-large, route=hosted-eu, at 14:03:21. short dump below:
```
[14:03:21] REQ session=abc123 route=hosted-eu seq=0 prefix_tokens=27
[14:03:23] STREAM_TRUNCATE session=abc123 reason=client_eof truncated_tokens=3 provisional=true
[14:03:24] RECONNECT session=abc123 new_seq=0 route=fallback-lowcost
[14:03:25] STREAM_CONT session=abc123 seq=0 resumed_tokens=40 confirmed=true
[14:03:25] BILL provisional: 27+3 (prefix+trunc) route=hosted-eu
[14:03:26] BILL confirmed: 40 route=fallback-lowcost
```
mike: total visible charge ended up ~70 tokens but UI shows 27 + 40 (truncation counted separate) so customer got double-charged for the 3 truncated tokens.
jordan: is truncation being reported as provisional and then confirmed separately? that log looks like we never dedup provisional vs confirmed attribution.
ashley: right — provisional events are emitted on truncate so customers see an early provisional charge, then confirmed comes on resume. we usually reconcile but looks like reconcile missed this flow because route changed to fallback-lowcost.
sarah: ahh route change is the kicker. reconciliation groups by (session, seq) + route. if route differs, we treat as separate billing buckets. that explains split.
emily: we intentionally tag provisional with original route so ops can rollback, but when routing policy swaps route mid-request we don't rewrite the provisional tag. should we instead tag provisional with a session-global id that survives route hops?
ravi: that would help. current ledger key = {session, route, seq}. proposal: ledger key -> {session, seq, provisional_id}. provisional_id generated at first provisional emission. then confirmed matches provisional_id regardless of route.
mike: sounds reasonable. what are downsides? complexity in ledger + UI mapping?
jordan: UI needs to show both provisional and confirmed flow. if we join by provisional_id we can show a single net charge, but console historic views rely on route-level breakdown. we'd need to surface that the confirmed came on a different route.
ashley: also need to think about sampling/telemetry. dashboards aggregate cost by route — changing keys will alter historical totals unless we emit a route-attribute for confirmed events.
emily: low-effort quick fix: suppress provisional charge emission when stream truncates and a reconnect is likely (we can detect client EOF followed by immediate reconnect within few seconds). but that's heuristic-y and may hide useful provisional visibility for slow clients.
sarah: agreed. heuristics are brittle. prefer a robust idempotency match.
ops-bot: BillingAlert: provisional discrepancy detected for acct=acme-inc session=abc123 delta=+3 tokens :chart_with_upwards_trend:
\ravi: next steps I propose: 1) add provisional_id to truncate emission (short change) 2) adjust confirm path to match by provisional_id if present (medium) 3) console: add combined "net tokens" column and keep per-route attribution (small UI change).
mike: timeline?
emily: I can push the truncate-side provisional_id change in a PR today (small). need r/ from ravi for the confirm matching.
jordan: I'll prototype dashboard change (net tokens) with a derived column in analytics; shouldn't take long.
ashley: need tests: create e2e that simulates route swap mid-stream and assert ledger nets to single charge. add unit for ledger key match.
\ravi: I'll own confirm-side changes and ledger migration plan. will also add a metric: count of provisional events with unmatched confirmed after 5m.
sarah: add an alert in console if unmatched_provisional_rate > 0.1% over 1h for high-spend customers. ops-bot should post into incidents channel.
mike: awesome. thanks all. one more ask — can we backfill for acme-inc? they pinged support.
jordan: we can run a reconciliation job: join provisional events lacking confirmed by session and timeframe, attribute to confirmed if total tokens overlap by time window and mark refund. I'll schedule a run tomorrow.
emily: PR link: https://git.redwood.internal/p/trunc-provisional-id (WIP)
ashley: thanks. tagging @support for follow-up with customer. :thumbsup: 
mike: closing loop — please post PRs and I'll add to release notes for next patch.
emily: will do.
